newsitem.title: USA: AMR sees fuel costs hurting Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: AMR sees fuel costs hurting Q4 earnings.

text.p: American Airlines parent AMR Corp expects rising jet prices to dampen fourth quarter earnings, chief financial officer Gerard Arpey said Wednesday.
"Fuel costs are going to hurt us in the fourth quarter. If fuel prices don't come down, it could play a part next year," Arpey said in a teleconference with reporters.
Arpey said he expects fourth quarter fuel costs to be about 31 percent or $0.18 a gallon higher than last year.
"For the fourth quarter, fuel prices are probably going to take the top off earnings," Arpey said.
"We hedged to dampen the volatility, but rising costs will still hurt us," Arpey said.
Separately, AMR spokesman Tim Smith told Reuters that the company has hedged an estimated 15 to 20 percent of its fuel costs.

During the conference call, Arpey said the airline expects fourth quarter traffic to be flat-to-slightly-higher than last year. Traffic volumes have fallen from the strong levels seen over the summer, Arpey said.

Earlier on Wednesday, AMR posted third quarter earnings of $282 million or $3.06 per diluted share on revenues of $4.56 billion. The third quarter includes pre-tax costs of $21 million for a legal settlement with travel agents.
In the third quarter of 1995, AMR posted earnings of $229 million or $2.64 per diluted share on revenues of $4.44 billion. The 1995 results include after-tax charges of $4 million.
